text:
Ava: quick check — running into weird 401s when switching from env var to file-mounted secret in docker. works locally with `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=abc123` but inside container when i `cat /secrets/redwood_key` and set `AUTH_HEADER=$(cat /secrets/redwood_key)`, requests fail.
Sam: do you mean you put the raw key in the file (no newline)?
Ava: yeah i thought so but turns out the secret came from a mac dev who used pbcopy and pasted, so probably trailing newline. `curl -v` shows header `Authorization: Basic <base64>` but still 401.
Diego: classic. trailing newline can change base64. try `tr -d '\r\n' < /secrets/redwood_key` or `printf '%s' "$(cat /secrets/redwood_key)"` when building the header.
Ava: ahh, didn't think of CRLF vs LF. also question: for basic auth do we send `username:password` or `:apikey`? our SDK examples use `ApiKey:` vs the quickstart uses `:<api_key>` and i'm confused.
Sam: Redwood API accepts either as long as the decoded value is correct. historically we had `user:apikey` examples but the canonical is empty username + apikey as password (`:<API_KEY>`). that's what most clients use for third-party apis. But both work if backend decodes it.
Diego: note: some http clients will trim NUL/newline or add their own quoting. e.g. node `Buffer.from(apiKey+':')` vs `Buffer.from(':'+apiKey)` — little differences matter.
Ava: here's what i tried in node inside container:
```
const key = fs.readFileSync('/secrets/redwood_key','utf8')
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(':'+key).toString('base64') } })
```
-> still 401
Sam: try `const key = fs.readFileSync('/secrets/redwood_key','utf8').trim()` first. Also log `Buffer.from(':'+key).toString('base64')` and compare to the base64 you get locally.
Ava: ok `.trim()` fixed it. thanks. two follow-ups:
1) is it safe to recommend `trim()` in examples? might hide intentional leading/trailing spaces.
2) streaming + header weirdness: when we stream responses via fetch/axios, if the auth header has a trailing newline we occasionally drop connection mid-stream.
Diego: for 1) i'd recommend `.replace(/[\r\n]+$/,'')` or `trim()` in most quickstarts; docs should mention if secret contains whitespace it can be significant. for 2) header values with CRLF can break HTTP framing in some proxies. absolutely sanitize before sending.
Sam: add a short note in devex docs: "Secrets copied from Windows/mac clipboard may include invisible newline characters; trim when reading into headers" — and show typical one-liners for bash/zsh/pwsh.
Ava: i'll open a tiny PR with examples for curl/node/python. sample bash snippet i used:
```
API_KEY=$(tr -d '\r' < /secrets/redwood_key)
AUTH_HEADER=$(printf ':%s' "$API_KEY" | base64)
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $AUTH_HEADER" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
Sam: perfect. also add a ci check in our docker builds to `hexdump -C /secrets/redwood_key | head` to catch trailing CR/LF in onboarding images.
ci-bot: build image debug-qa started for devex/secret-quirk — logs -> https://ci.redwood.internal/34/logs
Diego: tiny nit — in some languages (ruby/openssl) the base64 encoder adds line breaks unless you use the no-wrap option. good to mention `-w0` / `Base64.strict_encode64` variations.
Ava: great, thanks all. PR incoming. :thumbsup:
